target.censoring: 1873/37137 rows (5.04%) sit exactly at the upper bound 5.00001 — target is right-censored, not merely skewed

test_window.evidence: no date/time column in any file; id is a single contiguous integer range split at 37137 (train 0..37136, test 37137..61895), which encodes row order not time; test Latitude/Longitude span (32.55..41.95) is identical to train, and all 8 feature columns are static geo/demographic attributes of a census block. Nothing in the schema or config.yaml description ('Predict median house value (California Housing)') indicates a temporal or grouped holdout.

split_policy.scheme: shuffled KFold (5-fold), stratified on binned MedHouseVal (bins must isolate the 5.00001 censored mass, which is 5% of rows and would otherwise vary across folds)
split_policy.forbidden: none by time; but do NOT use plain unstratified KFold given the censored point mass, and do not group by lat/lon cell (test shares the same geography as train, so a spatial group split would understate the achievable score)
split_policy.rationale: TASK-TS-FUTURE does not trigger — no date column and no forecasting framing — so the time-split mandate does not apply here.

metric.name: RMSE
traps: censored target: unclipped predictions above 5.00001 or below 0.14999 are pure loss — clip predictions to the observed train range as a free post-processing step, and put the clip INSIDE the metric function so every blend candidate is scored on the clipped value

L2 metric means heavy-tail feature outliers (AveOccup max 502.99, Population max 35682, AveRooms max 28.84, AveBedrms max 5.87) drive squared error disproportionately — these are ratio features with tiny denominators, not data errors

RMSE-family blend weights have a closed form: use NNLS on OOF predictions, not a Dirichlet/random-search approximation (TASK-BLEND-DECOR evidence: search approximation error ~1e-5 can eat the real gain)

external_data.evidence: config.yaml special_rules sets external_data_allowed: false, pretrained_models_allowed: false, internet_access_allowed: false. Independently, no whitelist source joins: there is no country, no date, and no currency column, so World Bank (country x year), holiday calendars (country x date), ISO tables (country), ECB rates (currency x month) and OWID COVID (country x date) all lack a derivable join key. The only covariate the target plausibly depends on that is absent — finer-grained location context — has no whitelisted source.

data_level: geo interaction features from Latitude/Longitude: rotated coordinate pairs (45deg/30deg), lat+lon and lat-lon sums, distance to the California coastline proxy and to major-metro anchor points derivable from the data itself (e.g. k-means cluster centroids over lat/lon, then distance-to-each-centroid)

k-nearest-neighbour target encoding over (Latitude, Longitude) computed strictly out-of-fold — the strongest signal in California-Housing-shaped data is spatial, and the 8 raw columns expose it only as two bare coordinates

ratio/consistency features implied by the aggregate construction of the columns: AveRooms/AveBedrms, Population/AveOccup (implied household count), AveBedrms/AveRooms, MedInc x AveRooms (income per room), Population x AveOccup
outlier-robustness transforms for the long-tailed ratio columns (log1p on Population, AveOccup, AveRooms) as an alternative feature view for a decorrelated blend member
model_level: L2 objective throughout — metric is RMSE, so TASK-MAE-METRIC's L1 rule explicitly does NOT apply here
clip predictions to [0.14999, 5.00001] as an in-metric post-processing step for every candidate
GBDT trio (LightGBM / XGBoost / CatBoost) as the core pool — all-numeric low-dimensional tabular is their home turf

TASK-BLEND-DECOR: the GBDT pool will be variance-dominated; add one shallow heavily-regularized bias-dominated member from a different library family (regularized linear on engineered geo features, or a small MLP over standardized inputs) as a decorrelator before optimizing weights
blend weights via NNLS closed form on OOF, not Dirichlet search (RMSE-family)
optionally a two-part treatment of the censored mass (classifier for at-cap vs regressor below cap) as a diverse member — but only if the plain clipped regressor's OOF shows systematic bias near 5.0

rejected_task_priors.reason: no date column, no forecasting framing, contiguous id split with identical train/test geo support
no daily-resolution series and no store/product/country keys
all 8 feature columns are float64 numeric; zero categorical columns
8 columns x 37137 rows — rows greatly exceed columns, the opposite regime
single scalar target, no grid/sequence output
metric is RMSE (L2), not an MAE/SMAPE/quantile family metric

downstream_checks_for_stage_1: verify the iid hypothesis: compare train vs test marginal distributions per feature (adversarial validation AUC should sit near 0.5; anything above ~0.6 refutes the iid prior and forces a re-derived split policy)
confirm the censored mass at 5.00001 and check whether any near-duplicate rows exist across train/test (synthetic-generation artefacts would change the CV design)
quantify how much of the target variance the bare Latitude/Longitude pair explains, to size the payoff of the spatial feature ideas above
not_recorded: public/private leaderboard split ratio — not stated in config.yaml and no leaderboard page was consulted
official competition rules text — only config.yaml's special_rules block was available; the external-data verdict rests on that block, not on the rules page

whether the data is synthetically generated from a source dataset and, if so, whether the source is permitted — the description says 'California Housing' but no rules text confirms the generation process or its permissibility, and no whitelist source covers it
number of submissions already used against the daily limit of 5
